meta.description:
The CES/CENME (Execution Support and GeoBase) work center is a specialized element within the Engineering Flight (CEN) of a Civil Engineer Squadron, largely manned by 3E5X1 Engineering specialists and civilian equivalents . Its primary mission is to bridge technical project design, spatial asset management, and construction project closeout. Personnel in this section direct and execute engineering drafting (CAD/BIM), precise construction and topographic surveying, materials testing (soil, asphalt, and concrete), and contract construction surveillance . Furthermore, CENME serves as the gatekeeper for the project closeout lifecycle—receiving, reviewing, and archiving electronic "as-built" drawings, red-line contractor submittals, and DD Form 1354 real property transfer documentation to ensure every facility modification is permanently documented.

In tandem with project execution support, CENME operates and maintains the installation's GeoBase / Geographic Information System (GIS) architecture. Specialists collect field survey data using robotic total stations and GPS equipment, translating physical infrastructure into Spatial Data Standards for Facilities, Infrastructure, and Environment (SDSFIE) compliant datasets. By maintaining the Common Installation Picture (CIP), CENME tracks critical planimetric assets (airfields, roads, and building footprints) alongside underground and above-ground utility networks (water, gas, electrical, and storm systems) . This accurate spatial and record drawing repository directly enables safe excavation, emergency response mapping, and master planning across the entire installation.

meta.jhaNotes:
Major Hazards & Findings
Field survey operations present substantial struck-by hazards from vehicular traffic and taxiing aircraft on active flightlines, as well as biological risks including tick bites, insect stings, venomous snakes, and sharp vegetation when surveying in thick brush, high grass, or swamps. Active construction sites expose inspectors to slip, trip, and fall hazards, open trenches, moving heavy equipment, and overhead electrical power lines. In the lab, personnel encounter airborne nuisance dust and crystalline silica during aggregate sieving and sample preparation, along with high ambient noise when operating vibrating shakers or working in industrial flightline zones.

Bioenvironmental Engineering (BE) Survey Notes
BE industrial hygiene surveys for 3E5X1 operations primarily evaluate ambient noise exposure during mechanical soil preparation, sieve shaking, and airfield operations, as well as airborne respirable dust and crystalline silica concentrations during soil processing. BE periodic monitoring verifies that shop dust exposure remains below regulatory limits and evaluates whether administrative rotations, dust collection, or particulate respirators are required during prolonged aggregate sieving.

Controls & Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
Hazards are managed through strict job safety controls and personal protective equipment. Field personnel must wear ANSI Class 2/3 high-visibility vests, ASTM F2413 safety-toe boots, eye protection, and long pants/sleeves with insect repellent when working in dense vegetation to protect against ticks and thorns. Work in dusty environments requires proper ventilation, dust extraction, or NIOSH-approved N95 particulate respirators, and hearing protection must be worn during noisy laboratory or flightline tasks.

Special Restrictions & Prohibitions
Personnel must possess a valid Airfield Driver’s License (AF Form 483) and maintain two-way radio communication with the Air Traffic Control Tower before entering the airfield or Controlled Movement Area (CMA). All outdoor surveying must cease immediately upon notification of lightning within 5 nautical miles. Personnel must identify and maintain a safe clearance distance from overhead high-voltage power lines when setting up GPS survey rods, leveling rods, and tripods. Never enter an unshored trench exceeding 5 feet () in depth or enter any permit-required confined space without proper certification and an approved permit.

selectedModules.title: CPR Training
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 1
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Provide CPR and AED training before assignment where required, and refresh qualification before expiration.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Ensure designated responders maintain current certification and understand location and use of local AED assets under the unit mishap prevention program.

selectedModules.title: Active Shooter Response
selectedModules.reference: Installation emergency management guidance / local procedures
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Brief personnel on how to recognize an active shooter event, how to summon help, and how to apply local run-hide-fight guidance based on the facility layout.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use local emergency response procedures, shelter locations, and mass notification methods applicable to the duty location.

selectedModules.title: Government Vehicle / Utility Vehicle Use
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train vehicle operators on seat belts, speed limits, local traffic hazards, spotter use while backing, and restrictions on electronic device use while driving.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Brief operators on unit-specific government vehicle training requirements, local route restrictions, low-speed vehicle rules, and documentation of qualification.
selectedModules.trainingBasis: OSHA 2254 / Vehicle and Mobile Equipment Concepts

selectedModules.title: Risk Management Fundamentals
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train workers to identify hazards, assess risk, implement controls, supervise the task, and re-evaluate controls during and after operations.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use the DAF risk management process to discuss local hazard reporting, supervisor involvement, and integration into routine tasks.

selectedModules.title: Manual Lifting and Material Handling
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 20
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train workers on proper lifting techniques, team lifting, load assessment, and use of lifting aids to reduce musculoskeletal injury risk.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Provide verbal and written guidance on manual lifting, lifting devices, and local reporting actions for strain or overexertion symptoms.
selectedModules.trainingBasis: OSHA 2254 / Ergonomics and Material Handling Concepts

selectedModules.title: Fire Protection and Prevention
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards; local fire prevention plan
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train personnel on fire hazards, reporting procedures, extinguisher locations, evacuation routes, pull stations, and local emergency response actions.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use the JSTO and local fire prevention plan to brief workers on work-center fire hazards, alarm reporting, extinguisher use, and evacuation accountability.

selectedModules.title: Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 14; 29 CFR Part 1910 - Occupational Safety and Health Standards (General Industry Standards) Subpart I; 29 CFR 1910.132; 29 CFR 1910.133; 29 CFR 1910.135; 29 CFR 1910.136; 29 CFR 1910.138
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train each affected worker on when PPE is necessary, what PPE is necessary, how to properly don, doff, adjust, and wear PPE, the limitations of assigned PPE, and the proper care, maintenance, useful life, and disposal of PPE. Require workers to demonstrate understanding and proper use before performing work requiring PPE, and retrain when workplace conditions, job assignments, PPE types, or worker knowledge gaps make prior training obsolete.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use the work-center JHA, BE occupational health assessment, manufacturer instructions, DAFMAN 91-203 Chapter 14, and local safety office guidance to identify PPE requirements. Supervisors must ensure PPE is provided, used, cleaned, inspected, maintained in sanitary and serviceable condition, and documented in JSTO training records. Cover eye and face protection, head protection, foot protection, hand protection, protective clothing, and respiratory or hearing protection when those programs apply.
